unresolved_added: The three density-speed regimes lack stated domains, continuity conditions and empirical calibration.
The no-safety-interval premise overstates sensing and synchronization and omits braking, latency, failure and road condition.
Crossroads and toll delays are removed despite the network decision context.
Fixed traffic counts suppress route and demand response to changed travel times.
No lane changing conflicts with the dedicated-lane policy and merge-heavy network.
Identical four-meter vehicles omit trucks, buses and heterogeneous performance.
Combining both directions assumes symmetric, noninteracting demand.
Reaction distance alone omits braking distance and leader deceleration.
The four-meter grid, seven-cell speed ceiling and one-second clock have no discretization sensitivity.
The occupancy-derived speed is called capacity without served demand, throughput, censoring or spillback.
Reciprocal variance can diverge near zero and is called equilibrium without a stability definition.
Uniform independent arrival probabilities omit empirical arrival fit and entry blocking.
The source code can generate an initial speed of eight although the stated maximum is seven.
The transition rule has no simultaneous-update, collision-resolution or invariant specification.
One hundred repeats lack seeds, run-level variance and confidence intervals.
Four-percent and sixty-six-percent sensitivity judgments use endpoint changes without uncertainty.
Dual-Gaussian parameters, fitting data, criterion and goodness-of-fit are absent.
Hourly parameter adjustment conflicts with the claim of second-level density precision.
The schematic road geometry and color scale are not validated against held-out detector speeds.
The forty-five-percent tipping point is selected visually without a changepoint rule or uncertainty.
The sixty-eight-percent dedicated-lane crossover is visually interpolated from one allocation and one model.
Autonomous cars are barred from common lanes, a restrictive assumption that drives the lane comparison.
The ninety-five-percent decline motivates more lanes, but that repair is explicitly untested.
Infrastructure cost, enforcement, induced demand, equity and transition logistics are absent.
Claimed exactness from one-second updates is unsupported by grid or clock comparison.
Claimed stability is unsupported by reported run-level statistics.
Independent segment simulation breaks junction conservation; the source admits count loss or gain.
Route choice is omitted even though automation changes information and travel time.
The Conclusion presents approximate visual thresholds more firmly than the analysis warrants.
The Governor letter's 1.5-2-times claim is not reconciled with the roughly four-percent full-day velocity change.
Safety, fuel and emergency-response benefits appear in the letter without being simulator outputs.
MATLAB appendices are fragments without inputs, environment, seeds, tests, outputs or a runnable package.
